next_step: Finalize reserved GPU commitment number after 4-week POC and legal SLA redlines
notes:
Account background:
- Founded 2018, predictive claims automation for mid+large insurers. Heavy peak batch scoring at EOD plus interactive chat for claims agents.
- Evaluating dedicated GPU pool to cut token unit cost and hit latency SLOs for realtime agent workflows.
- Currently prototype on CloudModelX; migrating to Redwood for better production economics and routing features.

Recent timeline (key events):
- 2026-01-18: Intro call (Ethan / Rina) — overview of Redwood Dedicated, confirmed VPC requirement. (Gmail thread: thread:165732)
- 2026-01-26: Architecture deep-dive with infra + security. Security asked for SOC2 + KMS + data residency. (Drive: security-faq-orthus.pdf)
- 2026-02-03: Benchmark kickoff — baseline on 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (internal). Agreed POC scope: chat latency and bulk embeddings cost. (Fireflies: ff_2026_Orthus_call_0211)
- 2026-02-18: Internal pricing workshop w/ finance. Modeled 3 commit tiers and utilization assumptions. Shared draft cost model with Redwood.
- 2026-02-25: SLA negotiation call — legal flagged credits for underperformance + burst policy. (Jira INF-4321 opened for SLA exceptions)

Use-case & Requirements summary (as discussed):
- Primary: Agent chat for claims adjudicators (p50 target <= 60ms for 16-token responses; p95 <= 180ms). Strong tail latency sensitivity.
- Secondary: Daily batch embeddings for search/retrieval (~20M tokens/day peak), reranking pipelines during business hours.
- Throughput target: steady-state 600 concurrent chat sessions during business hours (~1200 rps small requests); peak batch throughput up to 4B tokens/day overnight.
- Cost sensitivity: high. Want committed-reserve economics to reach ~$0.0005 per token or cheaper at scale.
- Model preferences: multi-model routing (smaller distil for embeddings, larger for complex chat). Requires automatic fallback to cheaper variants when latency spikes or capacity constrained.
- Data controls: all inference must remain in customer VPC; audit logs retained 1 year; keys in customer KMS.

Cost modeling notes (customer-side estimates from finance; conservative numbers):
- Assumptions common across scenarios: baseline GPU equivalent = A100-40GB, price proxy from Redwood draft. Expected utilization friction (scheduling, KV cache warming) - assume 60% effective utilization on average.
- Scenario A (Conservative low-commit): commit 4 GPUs reserved. Avg utilization 45% (expected growth lag). Estimated monthly cost: $28k. Estimated token throughput/month (conservative): 300M tokens. Implied cost/token = $0.000093 (~$93 per 1M tokens).
- Scenario B (Mid commit optimized): commit 12 GPUs. Avg utilization 65%. Monthly cost: $78k. Token throughput/month: 1.2B tokens. Implied cost/token = $0.000065 (~$65 per 1M tokens).
- Scenario C (Aggressive scale + Optimize): commit 24 GPUs + Redwood Optimize recommended batching/kv caching. Avg utilization 78%. Monthly cost: $150k. Token throughput/month: 3.6B tokens. Implied cost/token = $0.000041 (~$41 per 1M tokens).
- Sensitivity notes: per-token unit economics improve strongly with utilization and caching; caching could reduce active token cost by additional 20-30% for chat prefixes. Burst credits and autoscale pricing need clarity — critical for peak-nightly embedding jobs.

SLA & procurement negotiation points (open):
- Requested: 99.9% uptime SLA, p95 latency SLOs scoped per model family, credits for SLA breach (sliding scale).
- Orthus wants a mechanism for true-up / rollback if utilization misses forecasts in first 3 months (to avoid over-commit penalty).
- Need explicit burst policy: ability to burst 20-30% above committed GPUs for 1-3 hour windows without 48h notice. Pricing for burst capacity TBD.

POC plan & deliverables (agreed):
- 4-week POC starting 2026-03-10. Objectives: reproduce p50/p95 latency on 16/64-token responses, run embedding nightly batch to validate cost per 1M tokens, validate KV cache speedups with live prefixes.
- Deliverable: POC report with measured latency percentiles, cost per 1M tokens, and recommended commit level with sensitivity bands.
- Acceptance criteria: p95 latency <= 3x of p50 for chat; embedding batch throughput target >= modeled baseline; cost per 1M tokens within 10% of modeled scenario B.

Quotes / paraphrases:
- "We can tolerate some underutilization in month 1 but need predictable unit cost by Q3." — VP Engineering
- "If Redwood can offer a true-up with a 60% utilization threshold, we can move to a 12–24 GPU commit." — Head of ML

Next steps (short):
- Rina to run benchmarking script (shared) on Redwood Dedicated trial cluster and return raw logs by 2026-03-20.
- Legal to circulate redline of SLA (Ethan to follow up with Redwood legal).
- Finance to finalize ARR band and internal approval by 2026-04-05.

Notes on differentiation & win criteria:
- Primary buying signals: predictable unit economics, tail latency guarantees, VPC + KMS controls.
- Redwood’s advantages to highlight in upcoming deck: model routing + automatic fallback, Optimize recommendations to lower unit cost, and per-token cost transparency (token-level billing + trace).

CRM-style shorthand closing summary:
- Risk: forecast uncertain for Q3; legal SLA still open.
- Likely commit if POC validates p95 & cost band (favored scenario B).
- Close target: 2026-04 (procurement team ready).
notes_short: Evaluation focused on reserved GPU commit sizing, unit economics per token across 3 scenarios, tail latency SLOs, and SLA/true-up negotiations. POC planned 4 weeks starting Mar. Key blockers: SLA language, burst policy, Q3 forecast uncertainty.
